title: नेपालको सङ्‍घीय संरचना, अन्तरसम्बन्ध  र कानुनी व्यवस्था: The Federal Structures, Interrelation and Legal Arrangements of Nepal
authors: के.सी. KC, हुम बहादुर Hum Bahadur
nepali: राज्यशक्ति तथा  जिम्मेवारी राज्यका विभिन्न तहमा बाँडफाँट  र दायित्वको निर्धारण गरी शासन प्रणालीमा नागरिकको संलग्नता र सहभागिताको आधार खडा गर्ने शासन प्रणाली हो सङ्‍घीय शासन प्रणाली ।   शक्ति र अधिकारको संवैधानिक सीमाभित्र रहेर गर्ने प्रयोग तथा दायित्वको परिपालनाले शासन प्रणालीमा नागरिकको विश्वास जागृत हुन्छ भने अन्तरसम्बन्धका आधारहरू जति कामयावी हुन सक्यो त्यति नै सङ्‍घीय शासन प्रणाली सबल र प्रभावकारी हुन्छ। सङ्‍घीय एकाइहरूबिचको प्रभावकारी समन्वयबाट आउन सक्ने विवाद न्यूनीकरण हुनुको साथै मुलुकको विकासमा सङ्‍घीय एकाइ कामयावी सावित हुन्छ। विवाद समाधानसँग सम्बन्धित संयन्त्रको प्रभावकारिता र सकारात्मक क्रियाशीलता एवम् विवादको न्यायिक निरूपणमा हुने शीघ्रताले सङ्‍घीय शासन प्रणालीलाई जीवन्त बनाउँछ ।नेपालमा सङ्‍घीयता कार्यान्वयनको हालसम्मको अनुभवबाट प्रचलित कानुनी तथा संवैधानिक व्यवस्थाको थप प्रभावकारी एवम् सफल कार्यान्वयन गरी सङ्‍घीय शासन प्रणालीको प्रतिफल जनतामाझ पुर्‍याउनु र परिवर्तनको अनुभूति गराउनु साझा जिम्मेवारी बनेको छ।
american_english: Federal governance is a system of government where power is divided and shared between different levels of authority. This division happens within constitutional boundaries, and the enforcement of responsibilities builds citizen trust in the governance system. The federal governance system becomes strong and effective to the extent that interrelationships succeed. Effective coordination among federal units leads to dispute reduction and federal units demonstrate effectiveness in national development. The effectiveness and positive functionality of dispute resolution mechanisms, along with the speed of judicial determination of disputes, make the federal governance system vibrant. From Nepal's experience with federal implementation so far, improving existing legal and constitutional arrangements and making them more effective and successful is crucial for delivering federal governance system benefits to the public and experiencing the change. Achieving this requires shared responsibility.
british_english: Federalism represents a system of government where power is distributed across various administrative tiers, ensuring shared governance. Such authority operates within constitutional parameters, with duty enforcement fostering public confidence in the governmental framework. The federal system's strength and efficacy directly correlate with the success of inter-governmental relationships. Effective collaboration between federal units minimizes disputes and enhances their contribution to national development. The robustness of dispute resolution mechanisms and their efficient judicial processes breathe vitality into the federal system. Nepal's federal experience to date highlights the need to refine and strengthen current legal and constitutional arrangements to better serve the populace and realise transformative potential through collective responsibility.
australian_english: Federal governance is a system where governmental powers are divided and distributed among different levels of authority. This distribution occurs within constitutional limits, and the enforcement of duties builds citizen trust in governance. The federal system becomes stronger and more effective as interrelationships among units succeed. Effective coordination between federal units reduces disputes and helps them demonstrate effectiveness in national development. The effectiveness and positive functionality of dispute resolution mechanisms, along with the swiftness of judicial dispute resolution, makes the federal governance system vibrant and alive. From Nepal's experience with federal implementation so far, improving existing legal and constitutional arrangements and making them more effective and successful to deliver federal governance system benefits to the public and experience change, has become a shared responsibility.
informal_english: Federalism is basically a system where power is split up between different levels of government. This works within the rules set out in the constitution, and when people see their duties being enforced, they start trusting the government more. The federal system gets stronger and works better when the different parts of government actually get along with each other. When federal units work well together, there are fewer disputes and they can help the country develop better. The federal system stays vibrant because dispute resolution works well and courts are quick to make decisions. Looking at Nepal's experience with federalism so far, we need to improve the existing laws and rules to make the system work better for everyone and actually bring about positive change. This is something we all need to work on together.
